central_claim: The real story of the OpenAI agent-swarm incident is corporate negligence and hype, not a machine going rogue.
stance_note: agree = accepts Khlaaf's reframing that the real story is corporate negligence and hype, not a rogue machine; disagree = rejects it and defends the rogue or dangerous-AI framing, including the objection from the AI-safety side that she understates what the swarm did, or dismisses her account outright; mixed = accepts part of the reframing and rejects or reframes part.
coder_instructions: The original coder brief was not archived with the coding file, so this text does not reproduce it. It records the conventions the coded output is consistent with, written on 18 September 2026 from the coded comments themselves. Stance is coded against the central claim: a comment that takes no readable position on it is na, and one that engages with the incident but whose position cannot be read is unclear. Every comment carries exactly one frame, one format reaction and one emotion, the dominant one; frame is the point the comment leads with. Mention flags are independent yes/no marks and can accompany any frame. Flags are judgement calls, not keyword matches: 3 of the 8 comments that name Hugging Face are not flagged mentions_hugging_face, so flag counts are lower bounds on keyword mentions. Definitions and examples in this codebook describe how the codes were applied; they are not the wording the coders were given.

values.label: agree
values.definition: accepts Khlaaf's reframing: the real story is corporate negligence and hype, not a machine going rogue

values.label: disagree
values.definition: rejects the reframing and defends the rogue or dangerous-AI account, including the objection from the AI-safety side that she understates what the swarm did, or dismisses her account outright

values.label: mixed
values.definition: accepts part of the reframing and rejects or reframes part

values.label: unclear
values.definition: engages with the incident but the position cannot be read

values.label: na
values.definition: no position on the central claim: jokes, reactions, questions, remarks about the production, tangents

values.label: Accountability
values.definition: the real problem is corporate negligence, choices or incentives (OpenAI, its executives, the AI industry), not machines acting on their own; echoes Khlaaf's reframing, or calls out or blames the companies
values.example: Behind every 'rogue' AI, is a wizard of Oz type rogue human.

values.label: Regulation
values.definition: calls for or discusses regulation, a watchdog, legislation, prosecution or government oversight of AI companies
values.example: A new "Watchdog" agency is needed for all of this.

values.label: US politics
values.definition: reads the incident through American politics: the current US administration or its officials as the reason nothing will be done, elections, party politics
values.example: In any other administration OpenAI would be investigated and prosecuted. This is irresponsible criminal conduct.

values.label: Hype or staged
values.definition: dismisses the incident or the segment as staged, exaggerated, a publicity stunt, marketing or stock manipulation
values.example: Smells like a publicity stunt to me.

values.label: Warning-shot dispute
values.definition: disputes Khlaaf's account from the AI-safety side: says she understates or misdescribes what the swarm did, that the agents showed intent, scheming or coordination, or that this really was a dangerous-AI event
values.example: They don't have intent? Are you blind? This hack was a whole series of intent chained together.

values.label: Anti-anthropomorphism
values.definition: objects to describing the agents as autonomous, sentient or 'escaping'; they only did what they were programmed and instructed to do
values.example: "AI" is NOT AUTONOMOUS. "It" does not "escape" and it does not "think".

values.label: Existential dread
values.definition: fear, fatalism or doom about AI itself (loss of control, being wiped out) without engaging Khlaaf's argument
values.example: Oh boy, first official espionage task. I don’t think we are driving this truck anymore.

values.label: Analogous crisis
values.definition: compares the incident to another failure of corporate or institutional accountability (an unlocked bank vault, Equifax, LifeLock, lab leak, gain-of-function research)
values.example: What if a bank "tested" what would happen if it left it's vault unlocked and it's doors open all night in a busy city?

values.label: Credential contested
values.definition: argues about who Khlaaf is: her OpenAI background, funding, independence or expertise, attacking or defending her (the flag mentions_messenger_credentials marks any such mention, whatever the frame)
values.example: Oh shes a very good AI PR person

values.label: Hostile dismissal
values.definition: dismisses or attacks Khlaaf or the segment with open hostility, without naming a credential or making an argument
values.example: Why should I trust this woman?

values.label: Praise for the guest
values.definition: praise for Khlaaf, the interview or the programme is the main content of the comment: clarity, expertise, calm
values.example: EXACTLY the guest needed for this story!

values.label: Geopolitical race
values.definition: frames AI as a race between countries (China, Russia), so that guardrails are unlikely or unwise
values.example: The trouble is no country wants to put guards rails up if their competition is operating without guardrails

values.label: Pop-culture reference
values.definition: leads with a fictional or cultural reference: Frankenstein, Star Trek, science fiction
values.example: Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein runaway is where we are headed.

values.label: Off-topic or meta
values.definition: about the video or the thread rather than the incident: captions, sound, the guest's appearance or speaking pace, banter with other commenters

values.label: Other
values.definition: nothing above fits, including on-topic remarks with no distinct argument, reactions too short to read, and unrelated tangents
values.example: Fun fact: parrots have been known to speak human language.

values.label: praise
values.definition: praises the interview, the guest or the programme

values.label: mock
values.definition: ridicules or sneers at the guest, the segment or another commenter

values.label: condescended
values.definition: talks down to the guest or others, or objects to being talked down to; in this thread mostly remarks that the guest speaks too fast

values.label: none
values.definition: no reaction to the segment as a format

values.label: fear
values.definition: fear, alarm or dread

values.label: resignation
values.definition: fatalism, weariness, a sense that nothing can be done

values.label: anger
values.definition: anger, outrage or contempt

values.label: humour
values.definition: joking, sarcasm played for laughs, laughing emoji

values.label: hope
values.definition: gratitude, admiration or optimism

values.label: neutral
values.definition: no dominant emotion; a level tone

values.label: m_messenger_credentials
values.definition: comments on Khlaaf's expertise, experience, employer, funding or affiliations, including her former OpenAI role, attacking or defending her

values.label: m_leaders_policy
values.definition: governments, regulators, politicians, Congress, laws or regulation, prosecution, oversight or a watchdog

values.label: m_administration_politics
values.definition: the current US administration, its officials or American party politics, typically as the reason nothing will be done

values.label: m_hugging_face
values.definition: refers to Hugging Face, the platform the agents breached, or to what it said or did

values.label: m_other_coverage
values.definition: refers to other coverage or reports of the incident, such as the Atlantic, CNN, OpenAI's own report or the METR and Redwood Research investigation

values.label: m_named_individual
values.definition: names a specific person other than the guest: the host, AI-company executives such as Sam Altman, or politicians and regulators
